name: btn
description:
The one button. Every affirmative, neutral, destructive and marketing action on every surface is this unit with a different variant.

The state design follows a reference set whose good idea is that each state changes the FILL and adds a RING — a halo just outside the edge, in the fill's own colour — rather than nudging opacity. A ring reads at a glance and at any size, survives a colourblind eye because it is a shape, and cannot be confused with the focus ring, which sits tight on the edge in sunflower.

base.$description: Fully rounded, and the only thing in the system that is — a stadium reads as pressable at a glance and nothing else on the page shares the shape. FLAT: no gradient. A wash across a 2.5rem control is invisible at rest and muddy in every state that changes the fill under it, and a button's depth should come from its ring and its shadow, which the eye can actually see.
base.transition: background var(--duration-quick) var(--ease-out), border-color var(--duration-quick) var(--ease-out), box-shadow var(--duration-quick) var(--ease-out), transform var(--duration-quick) var(--ease-out)

primary.$description: the one main affirmative action on a surface.

secondary.$description: neutral. An outline and dark text, never a coloured fill — a secondary action carrying a fill competes with the primary beside it.

danger.$description: destructive. The same variant on the trigger AND on its confirm dialog — red in one place and blue in the other is the bug this rule exists to stop.

ghost.$description: no chrome at all, for a tertiary action inside dense UI.

accent.$description: the marketing call to action — sunflower, the one place the brand shouts. Distinct from `primary` on purpose: primary is the main affirmative action on a form, accent is the thing the page is FOR.

unavailable.$description: not offered yet. NOT `disabled`: disabled means you may not, and this means there is nothing here to press. A muted fill rather than a dimmed primary, because dimming a primary reads as a control that failed rather than one that has not arrived.

icon.$description: Icon only. Square rather than stadium-wide, because a pill around a single glyph is mostly empty space — but still fully rounded, so it stays visibly the same family as every other button. The label lives in `aria-label`: an icon button with no accessible name is a button a screen reader announces as nothing at all.

success.$description: The end of a flow — a name claimed, a payment taken. It exists because a success that reuses the primary fill says 'press me again', which is the last thing it means.

lg.$description: a section CTA. 2.75rem clears the 44px touch target with room to spare.

xl.$description: the one submit a page is built around — the name check.

hover.$description: A ring and a lift. The ring is the reference set's idea and it is a good one: a halo just outside the edge, in the button's own colour, which reads at any size and does not depend on telling two similar fills apart. It is a `box-shadow` rather than an outline so it can coexist with the focus ring, which is an outline and sits tight on the edge.

focus.$description: The system focus ring: sunflower, 1px, tight on the edge. Deliberately a different shape from the hover ring, so focus and hover are never mistaken for each other.

active.$description: Pressed: the ring stays, the lift goes, and the shadow collapses — the button settles onto the surface it was floating over.

disabled.$description: Flat and quiet, not a dimmed slab. Reducing a filled button to 55% opacity over a cream page produces a muddy grey that reads as a control that failed rather than one that is not available yet — so the fill is dropped instead of faded.

loading.$description: Full strength with the ring showing, so an in-flight action reads as busy rather than unavailable. Reusing the disabled treatment says 'you cannot do this' when it means 'this is happening'.

reducedMotion.$description: The press feedback goes; the control still responds. Never `animation:none` as a blanket — a button has no entrance animation to lose, but the rule is written per unit because for others it would remove the very thing that reveals the content.

badge.$description: The circular affordance at the trailing edge — the reference set's other good idea. It is where a spinner goes while loading and where a chevron goes at rest, so the button's right side has a fixed place for state instead of the label shifting when one appears.

a11y.keyboard: Enter and Space activate. Tab reaches it. Disabled removes it from the tab order.
a11y.notes: `loading` deliberately keeps full opacity and swaps the cursor: an action in flight must not read as unavailable. aria-busy carries the announcement.
